overrideReason: All 3 automated attempts ran without SOSOVALUE_API_KEY provisioned (a real credential-provisioning gap, confirmed and fixed: the owner signed up and the key is now stored in .env.local and as a GitHub secret). Attempts 1-2 failed on unrelated issues; attempt 3 reached 8/9 with two real, legitimate findings from the verifier: (1) the story's own C9 live test's main assertion was a tautology (`result.value == result.value`, always true regardless of what the fetcher returns) - a real defect in the test's own substance, not the fetcher; (2) a claim that the fetcher is 'not wired into any pipeline entry point' - re-examined against this project's own established precedent (PRD-007's US-701, the analogous single-vendor fetcher story for Coin Metrics) and found to be an out-of-scope judgement: single-fetcher stories in this project are consistently fetcher-scoped only, with pipeline wiring deliberately deferred to a separate integration story (US-707 for PRD-007, US-807 here) - confirmed by reading US-701's own criteria, none of which required pipeline wiring either. Fixed the real, in-scope defect: rewrote the tautological live test with genuine assertions (Decimal type, non-empty reference period in the real YYYY-MM-DD shape, published_at timezone-aware and not in the future). Running this fixed live test with the now-provisioned real credential surfaced two further real, previously undiscoverable defects: SoSoValue's actual live API returns money fields (total_net_inflow, total_value_traded, total_net_assets, cum_net_inflow) as JSON floats, not the long-decimal strings the original research/docs examples described (confirmed live, 2026-09-28) - the schema's StrictStr fields rejected every real response outright. Also found an undeclared top-level `details` field (always null so far) that extra="forbid" was rejecting. Fixed both: schema fields changed to StrictFloat plus an optional details field; the fetcher's _parse_money now converts via Decimal(str(value)) rather than Decimal(value) directly, since the latter would preserve a float's own binary imprecision (Decimal(0.1) != Decimal("0.1")) and drift PRD-002's determinism golden files. Updated every offline mocked test fixture (summary_row, sosovalue_payload) from string to float money values to match the corrected, real schema, and rewrote the precision-round-trip test to test the actual risk (float-to-Decimal conversion via str(), not a fabricated 36-digit decimal string that a JSON float could never actually carry in the first place). Verified: uv run mypy ingest --strict clean, uv run ruff check clean, uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" (319 passed), and the corrected live test genuinely passes against the real endpoint for all three supported assets (BTC/ETH/SOL), each returning real, distinct Decimal values.

results.note: fetch_etf_net_flow reads SOSOVALUE_API_KEY via os.environ, sent as the x-soso-api-key header, never hardcoded - confirmed by direct code review and the offline auth tests.

Live-verified for real, post credential provisioning: fetch_etf_net_flow('BTC'/'ETH'/'SOL') each returned a real, distinct SosoValueEtfFlowOk with a real Decimal value from SoSoValue's live summary-history endpoint.
fetch_etf_net_flow returns Error(NOT_DEFINABLE) for BNB, detail naming SoSoValue's API symbol enum not including it - confirmed by direct code review and the offline test for this exact scenario.

Money fields parse as Decimal via str(float) conversion, never a raw float - confirmed by the corrected offline test (test_money_round_trips_via_str_conversion_without_binary_float_noise), which now tests the real risk (float precision) rather than a fabricated string-precision scenario a real JSON float response could never actually produce.
A reported net-flow of exactly 0.0 persists as Ok(Decimal('0')), not Unavailable - confirmed by the offline test for this exact scenario.
An HTTP 429 returns Error(FETCH_FAILED) with the status in the detail, no retry - confirmed by the offline test for this exact scenario.

The response schema uses extra="forbid"; a malformed/reshaped response is rejected - confirmed by the offline test for this exact scenario, updated to retype total_net_inflow to a string (now genuinely invalid, matching the corrected float schema) rather than the old, now-backwards retype-to-float case.

tests/test_sosovalue_fetcher.py::test_live_sosovalue_request_returns_real_etf_flow_data_for_one_asset, rewritten with real assertions (Decimal type, real date-shaped reference_period, timezone-aware non-future published_at) and re-run fresh with the real, now-provisioned SOSOVALUE_API_KEY: PASSED against the live endpoint.
`uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` re-run fresh against current HEAD: 319 passed, 54 deselected, exit 0. mypy --strict and ruff both clean.

note: All 9 criteria independently verified. This story's real path to done required a provisioned credential (now handled) plus fixing one genuine test-substance defect (a tautological assertion) and two genuinely undiscoverable-without-live-data schema defects (float-not-string money fields, an undeclared details field) - exactly the class of finding this project's discipline of live-testing before trusting research/docs exists to catch. The verifier's separate concern about pipeline wiring was examined against established project precedent (PRD-007's US-701) and found to be correctly out of this story's scope; that wiring is US-807's job.
